description:
FILED s538a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-12) beside #3618.  #3618 (s538a) made every OPENER's install slot (`%p-fh-place-check`: open, sysopen, opendir, pipe, socket, accept) die "Not a GLOB reference" for a box holding a reference that is not a handle (`%p-stat-handle-shaped-p` false, `ref` non-empty).  The USE slots are the same rule in perl (rv2gv) and were not touched.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on main 23f0f917 and the s538a tree alike; scratch/s538a/pr/useslot.pl in the s538a worktree):
    my $x = sub { 42 }; my $o = \$x;
    print $o "hi" / printf $o "%s", "hi" / print {$o} "hi" / close $o /
    my $l = <$o> / eof($o) / binmode $o / fileno($o)
  perl: every one dies "Not a GLOB reference"; PCL: every one returns ("ok"), the print writing nowhere visible.

FIX SHAPE (not started): the handle-USE resolution (`%p-fh-arg` / `%p-resolve-fh`, the print family's `:fh` slot) asks the same two facts %p-fh-place-check asks -- a box whose payload is not handle-shaped and whose `ref` is non-empty -- and dies.  CAUTION before widening: find every PCL representation that a handle slot legitimately receives (IO::Scalar / IO::String objects, tied-handle objects, a dirhandle, a socket object, a blessed glob) and probe each vs perl; `%p-stat-handle-shaped-p` is the one designator predicate.  BAR: the eight rows above + the controls (a glob, a glob ref, an open lexical handle, a blessed IO::Handle, a tied handle) vs perl; a Pl/t row beside Pl/t/open-modes-01.t row 11; the FULL sweep (a `cl/` handle-resolution change).

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- every slot as filed (silent): with `my $x = sub { 42 }; my $o = \$x;` -- print $o / printf $o / print {$o} / close $o /
  <$o> / eof($o) / binmode $o / fileno($o): perl dies "Not a GLOB reference" in each, PCL returns ok from each.
  Only a program perl itself kills reaches it (a handle slot given a code ref): it ranks low.
LABEL: silent (already in the subject).

=== DONE (s543n, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24; WIP 7 dabbb78e) ===
#3618's predicate is ONE function, %p-non-handle-ref-p (a box holding a reference whose payload is not handle-shaped),
asked by the opener's place check and -- on a MISS only, so no handle arm pays -- by p-get-stream (print printf say
readline eof binmode fileno seek tell flock read sysread syswrite getc), %p-close-impl and select, through
%p-fh-ref-designator: an object whose class overloads `*{}` is the glob the overload returns (PCL wrote nowhere before:
`print $ov "x"`, `fileno($ov)` now perl's), every other reference dies "Not a GLOB reference" (trappable).
truncate / stat / -f read a reference as a PATH (false, no death), as perl.
Probes scratch/s543n/probes/pG1.pl (19 slots x 4 reference kinds) = perl; pG2.pl controls (glob, glob ref, lexical,
IO::Handle, tied, a name string, closed handles, *{} overload, truncate / openhandle / -f / stat / select of a ref)
= perl except undef in print (#1421, its own task) and a reference as a DUP source (filed #5423).
Guard Pl/t/open-modes-01.t row 14 (FAILS on the base).

LEFT (review n-21, 2026-11-25; rare, only where perl dies; the same family as #1421): an UNDEF variable in a handle use
slot -- `my $u; print $u "x"` -- runs silently (PCL: nothing written, true/undef answer); perl dies "Can't use an
undefined value as filehandle reference" (print {$u}: "... as a symbol reference").  Not built: %p-fh-ref-designator
answers NIL for undef by design (the closed-handle and never-opened answers differ per slot, #1421's measurement).


=== CLOSED (the reviewing session, 2026-11-27) === merged as MAIN-READY-111 0ab08642 (s543n, code fd21062e = the stop's 0d5a13e9 rebased); the full gate on merged main 380 files / 12,499 rows PASS (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/gate-0ab08642.log); the review probes 22 of 24 = perl on the final tree (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/probes-1124/rn: n-13 = #5121 left by design, n-21 = the undef-in-a-handle-slot residue appended to #4842's note and left); no live baseline row is keyed on this task (the companion rows it fixed left perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit in the batch).
